LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION- HOMONYMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms, part of Strand 6 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can you distinguish the meaning between two different words with the same spelling?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify homonyms for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish meaning between homonyms for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify homonyms for information,

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. distinguish meaning between homonyms for comprehension,

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment.

   Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to put together a collection of homonyms from the community,

2. create mind maps to identify the different meanings of the words,

3. construct sentences to bring a distinction in meaning between homonyms,

4. fill in gaps with correct words from a set of homonyms,

5. compose a paragraph with the homonyms to create distinct differences in meaning between the words,

6. share their work with peers for review. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to put together a collection of homonyms from the community,
2. create mind maps to identify the different meanings of the words,
3. construct sentences to bring a distinction in meaning between homonyms,
4. fill in gaps with correct words from a set of homonyms,
5. compose a paragraph with the homonyms to create distinct differences in meaning between the words,
6. share their work with peers for review. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner works jointly with others to put together a collection of

homonyms from the community.

• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: The learner follows simple instructions when filling in gaps with correct words

from a set of homonyms.

Values:
• Peace: This is promoted as the learner displays tolerance when working with peers to put together a collection of

homonyms from the community.

• Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays accountability by sharing their work with peers for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: The learner works harmoniously and tolerantly with peers to put together a collection of homonyms from the

community.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of homonyms to similar content in English.

1. identify homonyms for information,
2. distinguish meaning between homonyms for comprehension,
3. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment.
